editorial:
Imagine walking into your own bathroom and finding a random naked man in your shower. That is exactly how this wild ride starts for Luisa. She does the right thing and calls the cops, but things get weird fast when a psychiatrist named Alberto realizes the stranger is actually Paolo, Luisa's husband. The catch? Luisa has no idea who he is. Even crazier, she looks at Alberto and thinks he is her husband instead. It is a wacky, confusing setup that feels like a giant puzzle, and the vibe is mostly lighthearted and funny as the guys try to fix her memory.

You will love how the movie keeps you guessing without feeling too heavy. The acting is great, especially the chemistry between the three leads who play the confusion perfectly. While some parts of the plot move a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy comedies with a mystery twist, you should definitely check this one out. It is a hidden gem from the eighties. Since it is an older flick, you should try to find it as a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture, or look for a high-quality digital rental on Apple TV.
endingExplained: The big twist is that Luisa was not actually suffering from memory loss. She was pretending to be confused as part of a scheme. She wanted to trick her husband, Paolo, and the doctor, Alberto, to see how they would react. After all the stress and the attempts to cure her, it turns out she was just playing a game with their heads. The movie ends with the reveal that she had everything under control the whole time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school Italian comedies and plot twists.
